title: Function pointers, callbacks and callback parameters
learningObjectives: Explain the C concept and its rules.
Trace the example and describe data flow.
Identify relevant failure and boundary cases.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: A function pointer stores a pointer to a function with a compatible function type. It can be called through the pointer and passed to another function as a callback. The pointed-to function's parameter and return types must match the pointer type.
understand.whyItMatters: Callbacks let a function delegate a decision or operation to caller-supplied behaviour, supporting reusable sorting, event handling and strategy selection.
understand.analogy: Treat the operation as a clearly specified contract between the program and its data.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's type, lifetime, I/O and object representation rules.

explain.narrative:
A function pointer stores a pointer to a function with a compatible function type. It can be called through the pointer and passed to another function as a callback. The pointed-to function's parameter and return types must match the pointer type.

Check all return values, object lifetimes, types and preconditions. Enable compiler warnings and test expected as well as failure paths.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: operation is a pointer to a function accepting two int values and returning int. calculate invokes the supplied function without needing to know its implementation.

practise.guidedTask: Write the function-pointer type in words and trace the callback call.
practise.independentTask: Implement a function that accepts a comparison callback and uses it to select the larger of two integers.
hints: Function pointer compatibility depends on the full function type.
Do not cast incompatible function pointers to silence diagnostics.
Use typedef to make complex callback signatures easier to read.
